claim: Creative work recruits default and executive control networks together, though they usually oppose each other.
note: Review plus connectome and latent-variable studies agree. Evidence is correlational (neuro-c-12).

claim: Early idea generation couples default with salience regions, later stages couple default with executive regions (a switch, then control).
note: Same lab (Beaty, Silvia, Benedek) for all; independence is weak. Two tasks (DT, metaphor).

claim: Generation and evaluation are different modes: evaluation recruits control more, but the split is not clean in time.
note: Rests on two small studies (poets, art students) as reported in one review. neuro-c-13 shows blurring.

claim: Divergent thinking quality is predicted by both associative ability and executive ability (updating, inhibition, fluid intelligence), not by shifting.
note: Two labs. Supports pairing a loose associative step with a control step.

claim: Later ideas in a session are more original (serial-order effect), flattened by high fluid intelligence.
note: Human result. LLM version rests on one unopened preprint (neurocreat-b-21), credibility 35.

claim: Connectome models predict creative ability only weakly, and shrink outside the discovery sample.
note: One study counted by three lines. Useful as caution, not as a design basis.

claim: Divergent thinking and insight rely on non-overlapping brain regions; the two are different processes.
note: Two meta-analyses plus a review of 72 studies saying the literature contradicts itself, so no single region claim is safe.

claim: Insight differs from analytic solving in right temporal gamma bursts and in pre-problem brain state.
note: Same lab family (Kounios, Beeman), small samples, some lines are snippets. Treat as moderate.

claim: Most problems labelled insight are solved by ordinary analytic processing; impasse is rare (about 8%).
note: One study, n=115. Challenges the insight category itself.

claim: Incubation (a break) has a small positive average effect, d about 0.29 per secondary sources; one line records 0.41.
note: Same meta-analysis cited three times, so one independent source. Number conflict: 0.41 (a-16, fetched) vs 0.29 (b-10, c-04). Check the paper.

claim: Incubation helps divergent tasks more than insight tasks, and more after long preparation.
note: Single meta-analysis.

claim: An undemanding task during the break beats a demanding task or rest, mainly for old problems.
note: Baird 2012 experiment supports. neuro-c-05 and neurocreat-b-11 report no break-demand effect or failed replication.

claim: The mechanism of incubation is not covert unconscious work and mind-wandering content does not predict the gain.
note: Gilhooly review and Baird agree on no link, but neuro-a-22 speculates default-executive mixing. Mechanism open.

claim: Unconscious thought theory (deciding after distraction) fails to replicate.
note: Large replication, bias-corrected meta-analysis, a second replication. Strong. Do not add 'sleep on it' steps for decisions.

claim: The feeling of an aha raises belief in true and false statements, so insight feeling is a misleading heuristic.
note: Preregistered n=300 plus a preprint essay. neurocreat-b-13 finds some accuracy link for implicit problems, so partial contest.

claim: Brain stimulation (40 Hz tACS right temporal) raised verbal insight accuracy about 19-20%.
note: n=31 crossover; no transfer to agents.

claim: Intrinsic LLM self-correction without external feedback can lower reasoning accuracy.
note: Huang 2023 plus Lu 2025 (no gain from self-correction on creativity in code). Matches our always-doubt loss on single-answer tasks.

claim: Separating free exploration from constraint satisfaction in a two-phase prompt raised LLM diversity and novelty.
note: Preprint, abstract only. Matches our own NoveltyBench result.

claim: LLM help raises creativity during use but may hurt later unassisted creativity.
note: Human outcome, not agent design. Low relevance.

claim: LLM representations align with default mode network more as size grows; reasoning-trained variants shift toward analytic alignment.
note: One preprint, 2026. Speculative.

claim: Control network is not one thing: subnetworks couple differently with the default network and only one tracks creativity.
note: Beaty 2021 plus the review's goal-directedness caveat. Warns against a single 'critic' step.

claim: Deliberate, not spontaneous, mind wandering predicts creative performance.
note: Trait questionnaire, n=77, snippet only.
